lines: Half of all sports searches happen while the game is live.
And in twenty twenty-five, fifty-two percent of fans used generative AI, up from thirty-one.
Copilot already had the scores, the teams and the match state.
But when fans asked about a game, the answer was still mostly text.
So I turned the structure already in the sports data into a visual hierarchy.
The card answers the question at a glance, and deeper content waits for fans who want more.
Cricket has overs, tennis has sets, F1 has laps, and the NFL has downs.
One shared layer controls how every card reads, a sport layer controls what matters, and adding a sport became data mapping, not a redesign.
Then I designed every state, not just the final score.
Pre-game, live and post-game, plus the edge cases that break layouts, like rain delays, red flags and super overs.
The system shipped across four sports, and others built Copilot's broader sports experience on top of it.
When Copilot moved to a new design language in twenty twenty-six, the same cards carried straight into the new shell.
Consistency across surfaces is a system property, not a per-card decision.
